claims.claim: Brier-UDAM decomposes the paired Brier-risk difference exactly as DeltaR = DeltaM + DeltaD + DeltaL (mean-bias, dispersion, Brier-scale alignment).
claims.stance_target: paired comparison of probabilistic predictors via decomposition
claims.scope_conditions: paired binary prediction rules in same population
claims.quoted_support: For two rules evaluated in the same target population, the exact identity ΔR = ΔM + ΔD + ΔL holds, and the corresponding plug-in estimators reproduce the empirical paired Brier-risk difference exactly in finite samples.

claims.claim: Influence-function inference for first-order regular contrasts and a projection-based confidence procedure when first-order inference degenerates; projection intervals conservative.
claims.quoted_support: projection intervals retained coverage near degeneracy but were conservative.

claims.claim: In a 30-day hospital readmission analysis, models with similar held-out Brier risks had substantially larger and opposing dispersion and alignment contributions.
claims.quoted_support: models with similar held-out Brier risks showed substantially larger and opposing dispersion and alignment contributions, revealing cancellation that was hidden in the aggregate score.

breadth.confidence_families: not present (searched: language model, LLM; clinical risk prediction only)
breadth.benchmarks: Simulations and large public 30-day hospital readmission data (Abstract).
breadth.calibration_metrics: Brier risk decomposition; calibration, discrimination, information-based assessments said to address distinct questions (Abstract).
